question: ATS-2025 Table 100.6.3, sinusoidal VLF acceptance test for a 15 kV cable system, phase-to-ground, is:
choices: 21 kV rms for at least 30 minutes
explanation: The acceptance row is 21 kV rms, and the notes call for a minimum of 30 minutes (60 if the circuit is critical). 16 kV is the MTS-2023 maintenance value for 15 kV, not the ATS acceptance value. 56 kV DC is the extruded-dielectric DC table, which is a different test.

question: Table 100.6.6's worked note: Uo for a new 15 kV cable is:
explanation: Uo is phase-to-ground. 15 / √3 = 8.7 kV. 21 kV is the acceptance VLF withstand, not Uo. Tan-delta steps are 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 times Uo.

question: Charging current of a cable is proportional to frequency. Moving a withstand from 60 Hz to 0.1 Hz changes that current by about:
explanation: I = 2πfCV, so the ratio of frequencies is 60 / 0.1 = 600. That is why a VLF set can energize a long cable a 60 Hz set cannot. The voltage and the hold time still have to be the table values.
reference: Capacitive charging current; IEEE 400.2 / ATS Table 100.6.3 is the voltage table

question: A 15 kV shielded cable. Which VLF rms phase-to-ground voltages match ATS acceptance and MTS maintenance?
explanation: ATS-2025 Table 100.6.3 acceptance for 15 kV is 21 kV rms. MTS-2023 Table 100.6.3 maintenance for 15 kV is 16 kV rms. Both notes use a 30-minute minimum. 8.7 kV is Uo for a 15 kV system, not the withstand.
reference: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 Table 100.6.3; ANSI/NETA MTS-2023 Table 100.6.3

question: ATS Table 100.6.1, extruded dielectric shielded cable, note 2 says:
choices: DC testing is preferred after 5 years because it is gentler
After 5 years of service, DC testing is not recommended
DC testing is forbidden on all new cable
explanation: The note says after 5 years of service, DC testing is not recommended. New cable still has a DC column in that table, with a 15-minute hold, but service-aged extruded cable is not where you reach for DC first. VLF is the separate table.

question: PE-insulated cable, VLF tan delta, sinusoidal 0.1 Hz. Table 100.6.7.1 says tip-up (1.5 Uo minus 0.5 Uo) requires action when it is:
explanation: Acceptable tip-up is below 5 (in units of 10⁻³), further study is 5 to 80, and action required is above 80. If any one of standard deviation, tip-up, or mean lands in a worse column, the cable takes that worse grade. EPR uses Table 100.6.7.2, not this one.

question: ATS Table 100.6.3 sinusoidal acceptance voltage for a 5 kV shielded cable, phase to ground, is:
explanation: The 5 kV row is 10 kV rms. 21 kV is the 15 kV row. The notes still want at least 30 minutes, and a cosine-rectangular waveform is the rms value times √2.

question: For a cosine-rectangular VLF set, ATS Table 100.6.3 says to take the sinusoidal rms value and:
explanation: The note says cosine-rectangular waveforms use the table voltage times the square root of 2. Using the sine number on a cosine-rectangular set undervoltages the cable.

question: PE-insulated cable, tan delta in units of 10⁻³. A mean value that requires action under Table 100.6.7.1 is:
explanation: Mean at a step: acceptable below 4, further study from 4 to 50, action required above 50. Tip-up has its own 5 and 80 limits. One bad column sets the grade.

question: An EPR cable’s tan-delta mean is 40 × 10⁻³. Using Table 100.6.7.2, that result is:
choices: Acceptable, because PE’s action line is 50
Further study (35 to 120), not yet action-required
Action required, because PE’s acceptable line is 4
Invalid, because EPR uses the PE table
explanation: EPR’s own table: mean acceptable below 35, further study from 35 to 120, action required above 120. Grading EPR with the PE mean of 4 condemns a cable the EPR table still calls further study. Fill type can move the EPR numbers; unknown fill uses this table.

question: ATS Table 100.6.3 acceptance voltage for a 25 kV shielded cable, sinusoidal, phase to ground, is:
explanation: The 25 kV row is 32 kV rms. 16 kV is the MTS maintenance value for 15 kV, not this acceptance row. Hold at least 30 minutes unless the note’s 60-minute case applies.

question: Choosing a megohmmeter voltage for a 600 V cable when the manufacturer is silent means:
choices: The highest range on the set, to be sure
The Table 100.1 test voltage for that rating, 1000 V DC, not a 5 kV or 10 kV shot
explanation: Table 100.1 for a 600 V rating is a 1000 V DC test. The meter’s top range is not the specimen’s rating. A voltage lock on the set is how you keep from exceeding the voltage you actually chose.

question: IEEE 400.2 prefers VLF for many shielded extruded cables in the field because:
choices: DC hipot is gentler on aged XLPE
Charging current falls with frequency, so a portable set can energize a long cable
0.1 Hz raises the voltage stress on purpose above the BIL
Tan delta cannot be measured at 0.1 Hz
explanation: The 400.2-2024 introduction, which is not a numbered requirement of the standard, explains that charging current at 0.1 Hz is on the order of 1/600 of the 60 Hz value, so a portable set can energize a long shielded cable. ATS Table 100.6.3 is the acceptance voltage adapted from that guide, and the table’s DC note discourages DC on extruded cable after years in service.
reference: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.3.3.B.5.2 and Table 100.6.3; ref. IEEE 400.2-2024 introduction (charging current at 0.1 Hz)

question: When the manufacturer is silent, ATS 7.3.3.B.4 sets the one-minute jacket test at:
choices: At least 2 kV up to 35 kV cable, and at least 5 kV above 35 kV
The same voltage as the VLF withstand
explanation: The jacket test is not the insulation withstand. Up through 35 kV the floor in that sentence is 2 kV; above 35 kV it is 5 kV. Manufacturer data still wins when it exists.

question: ATS 7.3.3.D.2 says to investigate a cable shield whose resistance is:
explanation: The shield has to be continuous. More than 10 ohms per 1000 feet is the investigate line. A shield that reads open will not do its job for the withstand or for a ground-fault return.

question: An offline partial-discharge test on shielded cable passes ATS 7.3.3.D.8 when:
choices: Any discharge is present at operating voltage
There is no partial discharge at or below the threshold in the manufacturer’s data or in IEEE 400.3
The jacket ohms are above 10 per foot
The VLF set trips on overcurrent
explanation: Offline PD is judged against the manufacturer’s voltage threshold or IEEE 400.3. A trip of the withstand set is a failure of a different test. Record inception, extinction, location, and the phase pattern rather than a single beep.

question: In IEEE 400.3-2022 clause 3.1, partial-discharge inception voltage is:
choices: The voltage where repetitive discharges first appear as the voltage is raised
The voltage where discharges stop as the voltage is lowered
explanation: Inception is the first appearance on the way up. Extinction is the cease point on the way down. ATS 7.3.3.B.8 tells you to record both, along with location and magnitude. The withstand voltage is a different test.

question: ATS 7.3.3.D.7, for an online partial-discharge test of shielded cable, expects:
choices: A reported discharge from the cable at operating voltage
No evidence of partial discharge from the cable, with background noise kept out of the report
A turns-ratio test of the splice
explanation: Online, there should be no cable discharge. If something is there, record amplitude, repetition, and the phase pattern so internal, surface, and corona can be told apart. Background noise is not reported as cable PD.
